m2_acceptance.scope: M2's source contract on this machine, through the production entry points, on the model-bundle flow: a base trained, paused and resumed, a disease child finetuned from a base, paused and resumed and extended, the child measured by the disease protocol and served for the disease task. The real-data models are short trainings by the reference recipe that show the pipeline and its checks work; they are not models of serving quality, which is chosen by the established training and evaluation. Architecture, as the runs are built: the demo part trains the gatv2 encoder (the demo's model spec) and the real part the gatv2 encoder (the reference recipe's base spec, which R3 trains). Other encoder kinds are refused by the model-bundle builder and are outside this acceptance, their devices and precisions included, until the multi-architecture milestone. Precision, as the runs ask for it: the demo part's M2 and M9 run in mixed precision float16, as stated, and pass only with float16 in effect and a gradient scaler restored from the parent's state; the real part's R3 and R4 run in fp32, as the base recipe asks, with no mixed-precision claim. The run also carries contract M4's flow (T1-T6, RT1-RT3): a synthetic supplied cohort imported, measured, kept, registered and read back through the read-only view. That is a functional check of the flow and its refusals, not a measure of model quality, and not an institutional test, which waits for real data, its terms and a pre-declared protocol. It carries M5's acceptance where it runs headless too (A5, W1-W11, RW1-RW3): the environment against the lock beside the checkout, the server's lists, D8, CORS and the route guard on the service started as the launcher starts it, the GPU lock, and test and training jobs through the job runner, started and stopped; not the dashboard's layout or a browser session, and no long training. It carries the research comparison round's probes too (A6, L1-L8), on the demo workspace: each named component's native build identity and route, recorded and never compared with a version; a KG edge set taken from the demo base, measured by the KG link-prediction protocol through the measurement command and the job runner, its exposure, scores, pairs and summary checked against each other, and its refusals; a disease child measured by two protocols; a generated split imported, measured and registered; short disease, gene and patients-like-me children trained and measured on this device as regression cases, not studies; and the results export listing every record of that flow. Its figures are a functional check, never a comparison of models. Last, it records M1's served readings of the demo disease child (S1): the service's cold start, warm-up and steady-state request times and its process's memory, informational and never required, so no reading, however slow or large, leaves the acceptance incomplete, and nothing it reads is judged. Nor does its failure set the run's exit status.

cuda_allocator_peak.reason: torch keeps its allocator counters inside the server's process and no route of the service exposes them; a reading in the probe's process would describe the probe, not the server

definitions.allocator: the allocator variables in the environment the server process was started with (/proc/<pid>/environ), raw, null when absent: `state` "read" with them, or "not_obtainable" with its reason when that environment cannot be read or the process has exited
definitions.cold_start.seconds: the probe's clock from launching the service's process (uvicorn serving the application, as the launcher starts it; the process is the server's own) to its first /health answer. The application builds the configured pipeline in its startup, before the service accepts a connection, so this covers the interpreter's start, the imports, the dashboard's mount, reading the workspace and the checkpoint, building the model and moving it to the device. /health is asked every 0.5 s, so it reads up to that much late, and the seconds are rounded to 0.1 s (`_ProbeServer.wait_ready`). `state` "read" with them, or "not_obtainable" with its reason when /health never answered
definitions.counted: a request answered 200 with a JSON body whose served identity is the one the status reported at readiness; any other answer is a failure, by class, and a phase with one is incomplete. A request with no whole answer (timed out, reset or cut off) ends the readings: the server may still be working on it
definitions.cuda_allocator_peak: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated of the server's process: torch keeps it inside that process, and no route of the service exposes it
definitions.memory: the server process's VmRSS (resident now) and VmHWM (its peak resident size since the process started) from /proc/<pid>/status, in bytes, approximate as the kernel's RSS accounting is. VmHWM is never reset here, so it is the peak since the start, never one phase's. Whether a unified-memory device's allocations count in it is not established
definitions.readiness: before anything counts: the first /health answer (the cold start), /ready answering 200, and the status's served identity naming the child, the workspace and its dataset record by the digests this probe read, the disease task and the device asked for (`_assert_served_identity`). `state` "ready" with /ready's `ready_status`, or "not_ready" with `failed_at` ("health", "ready" or "served_identity"), its `reason` and /ready's `ready_status` once it answered. A service not shown ready is sent no request: what was read before stays, and every reading after is not taken
definitions.seconds: per counted request, the probe's clock (time.perf_counter) from sending one POST /api/v1/diagnose, on a new loopback connection, to reading its whole answer. The service answers after the disease head's scores are copied to the host, so on CUDA the time includes the device's work, synchronised by that copy in the server's process; the probe's process runs no part of the request, and no synchronise call is made in it
definitions.server_handler_seconds: per counted request, the answer's own inference_time_ms in seconds: the route's wall time from its start to the answer built, before it is validated and sent
definitions.steady_state: the requests after the warm-up, a fixed count, sent serially. Every request asks the same query, and the service keeps no result cache, so each answer is computed
definitions.warm_up: the first requests after readiness, a fixed count, whatever they took

not_covered: a peak per phase: VmHWM is not reset between phases (PLAN_B04 §7.3's reset pauses the server, and is not taken here)
system-wide memory and swap, a baseline before the launch, and the machine's OOM kills (PLAN_B04 §7.3's R0 and system counters)
a reload, and the old and new pipelines held together (PLAN_B04 §7.3's R3 and R4)
concurrent requests, a varied or largest-size workload, and repeats over several cold starts: one query, the same each time, from one cold start
the real workspace's children at deployment size, and gene and patients-like-me children: only D1's disease child on the demo workspace is served
